match.reason: The bank point teaches linking a text to your own experience with evidence from the text, but the new point asks students to compare first impressions with what closer study of the whole text reveals, which is a different idea.

draft.title: Personal response that develops
card: A personal response is your own reaction to a text: what you think, feel and notice. It starts with a first impression, formed from the opening or a first read.
Closer study means looking at the whole text and how it is built. You notice the ending, repeated images, and how characters change.
A strong response compares the two. It says what you first thought, what closer study showed, and why your view shifted, stayed the same or became more detailed.
Your ideas are backed by evidence from the text, such as a detail or a technique. A feeling with no evidence is only a first impression.
draft.remember: A strong response tracks how your view grows from a first impression to a view supported by the whole text.

a.q: Which sentence best shows a personal response that develops?
opts: I thought she was cold, but the ending showed her hidden grief
I liked the narrator from the start and I still like her
The narrator is cold and I did not enjoy the story at all
The narrator is in most chapters and speaks in first person
a.why: The first option compares a first impression with what the whole text revealed and gives a reason. The second names no change or evidence. The last two give a view or a fact without comparing.
a.clue: Look for a view that is compared with a later view.

b.q: Ravi first thought a novel's opening was dull. After finishing it, he wrote about how the slow start made the final chapters hit harder. What makes this a developed response?
opts: He links his first impression to what the whole text showed
He changed his mind, which always makes a response stronger
He says he finished the novel, so his view must be correct
He states that the opening of the novel was dull
b.why: Ravi compares his first impression with what the whole book revealed and explains the link. Changing his mind is not what makes it strong, because a view that stays the same can also develop with evidence. The comparison and reasons do the work.
b.clue: Ask what he compared, not only whether he changed.
